title: Testing International AI-Agreement Verification Mechanisms Against a Toy Adversary Model

original_idea.body:
# Testing International AI-Agreement Verification Mechanisms Against a Toy Adversary Model

**Problem:** 'Mechanisms to Verify International Agreements About AI Development' surveys verification mechanisms (compute monitoring, declarations, inspections) but does not provide a simple, reproducible way to reason about which mechanisms survive specific evasion strategies.

**Direction:** Build a small tabletop/game-theoretic model (a spreadsheet or short simulation) pairing each verification mechanism with a set of concrete evasion moves a non-compliant actor could take, and score detection probability and cost under stated assumptions. Run sensitivity analysis on which mechanisms are robust across adversary assumptions.

**Why it matters:** International coordination and treaty verification are core long-horizon governance levers; a transparent, re-runnable robustness model is valuable public infrastructure built with no lab resources. Light simulation, statistics.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Mechanisms to Verify International Agreements About AI Development' (arXiv:2506.15867, 2025) with a reproducible adversary-vs-mechanism robustness analysis.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon public infrastructure labs won't build, no internal access needed.

novelty.reasoning: Verification mechanisms surveyed; a reproducible adversary-robustness model may be open.
